content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (fallback target).**

- **What exists:** a servicing performance standard in §3.2(a) (reasonable care / same skill as for its own comparable receivables), and point-in-time Servicer reps in §6.1(a) on compliance with Law (ix) and compliance with the Servicing Procedures (x). Remedy machinery is limited to the Servicer's acquisition of affected Receivables, and §3.3(g) makes that the *sole* remedy for §3.2(b)–(d) breaches only.
- **Why it fails fallback:** no conformance-to-documentation warranty for the receivables systems/software or delivered reports, no warranty duration at all, and no repair, replacement or refund remedy. Per detection guidance, a missing express warranty is a deviation cured by insertion.
- **Cure:** one insert after §6.1(a)(x) adding a new (xi) Performance Warranty — 90-day software/systems conformance to documentation, 30-day services conformance, with repair/replacement or refund at the Issuer's option. Nothing beyond the four fallback elements was added (no survival tail, no disclaimer carve-out boilerplate), and the retained §3.3(g) sole-remedy clause is confined to §3.2(b)–(d) so it does not conflict.
